overall_reason: The lead picture is a real capture of Apple's 'Welcome to Apple Arcade' email (contact sheet #1), but the file is 591px wide shown at 894px, so its game art and body text are upscaled and soft.

score.reason: T-MATERIAL-SOURCE passes on real email captures, but T-IMAGE-SIZE fails on the lead capture at 0.66x and the thumbnails at 1.1x (IMG-009).

findings.where: lead email capture (div.jTWvec.dMMuNs > img), 1440 (tiles/1440-01.png, contact sheet #1)
findings.evidence: The capture file is 591 by 2556px shown at 894 by 3868px: density 0.66, upscaled about 1.5 times. On tiles/1440-01.png the headline 'You're Going to Love It Here' and the body paragraph have soft, haloed edges, and the wheat-field game art is blurred.
findings.before: the email the page is about, upscaled to 151% of its file width
findings.after: Capture the email at 2x its design width (1200px) and show it at no more than the design width times the screen density
findings.why: Visitors come to study the email's craft, and upscaling hides the type and image detail they came for.

findings.where: 'You might also like' cards, 1440 (tiles/1440-04.png, contact sheet #3 to #9)
findings.evidence: Each card frame is 325 by 650px while the captures run up to 359 by 4890px; the table marks seven as cropped, so each card shows only the top of a long email.
findings.before: tall email captures cut to a fixed 1:2 window
findings.after: Keep the top-crop but fade the bottom edge so the cut reads as deliberate
findings.why: A hard cut through a section looks like a broken image in a gallery of finished work.

strengths: The pictures are real email captures from named senders, not mocks.
The cards share one frame: 12px radius, 1px border, one size.
